messages:
ops-bot: Pager triggered: hosted-api-us-east - GPU pool 'hosted-rtu-pool-3' reporting node OOMs and provisioning failures. queue_size=12k, inflight=980, p95=3.8s, p99=9.2s. Autoscaler attempts failing with 403 quota error from cloud provider. Escalate to oncall. :rotating_light:

maria (oncall): I'm on it, pulling up dashboards. tagging @jonathan for provisioner help.

jonathan: on pager. I see the provisioner controller logs throwing repeated `CreateInstanceQuotaExceeded` and then `provisioner: timeout waiting for VM ready` retries. Cloud quota is at 100/100 for GPUs in region.

inge: any customer-facing errors yet? CS pinged me about timeouts from a handful of mid-market customers.

customer-success: multiple customers reporting slow responses and occasional 504s, highest impact for realtime apps (webhooks). Not seeing dropped requests in logs yet, mostly high backpressure and retries. 

maria (oncall): OK, immediate plan: 1) enable fallback routing to smaller-quantized model variant for non-enterprise routes 2) enforce short-term per-customer rate limit reductions 3) escalate quota request with cloud and try a soft quota-bypass for emergency allocations.

max: I can flip the routing flag. Which route? we have `hosted-default` and `hosted-lowlatency`. Suggest route lower tier => `hosted-compact-v2`. That reduces memory per model.

jonathan: do it. Also I'll restart provisioner controllers to clear stuck async operations: `kubectl -n infra rollout restart deployment/provisioner-controller` — doing now.

deploy-bot: Rolling restart initiated for deployment/provisioner-controller in namespace infra. Rollout ID: r-20240328-58.

inge: Can we also drop token limits temporarily for streaming sessions? Those are inflating queue processing time for p99.

kate: I'll apply a short-term policy change: reduce max_tokens_per_request from 4096 -> 1024 for non-enterprise API keys. Pushing patch to feature flags.

maria (oncall): Kate, push it and post the flag toggle command here. Also add a note for rollback.

kate: toggled flag `reduce_nonent_max_tokens_2024-03-28=on` via ops-console. CMD: `opsctl feature-flag set reduce_nonent_max_tokens_2024-03-28 true --env hosted-us-east`.

jonathan: provisioner restart showing pods coming up but one node stuck in `Init` with image pull backoff. Looking at cloud provider API — emergency allocation attempt returned `quota.exceeded` at 17:12:03. I've opened support case and requested accelerated quota for +50 GPUs.

maria (oncall): Good. Max, can you flip fallback routing now so new requests route to compact model? Include a message to dev docs so SDKs don't break.

max: done. CLI: `rdw-route set default --model=compact-v2 --region=us-east` — changes live. Monitoring traffic shift. p95 dropping to 1.1s for routed traffic, overall p95 trending down slowly. :thumbsup:

sre-bot: Noted change: route default->compact-v2. Observability rule triggered: backlog decreasing from 12k -> 6.1k in 7m.

jonathan: Restart cleared most stuck provisioner jobs, remaining failures are due to quota. Support case #CLOUD-9051 created. No immediate increase possible until quota approval or we free GPUs.

maria (oncall): Next mitigation: identify noncritical dedicated pools to evict less-active workloads and shift to dedicated reserved capacity (announce to teams). Jonathan, can you run `provisioner drain --pool=staging-gpu-1 --evict-grace=30m` and move those jobs?

jonathan: kicking drain. starting migration tasks.

customer-success: update: top-tier enterprise customers reported minimal visible impact after fallback; smaller self-serve customers saw higher error rates earlier but most recovered after routing change. We're sending a status note to affected customers now.

maria (oncall): Summary for pager: Root cause: sudden traffic burst + cloud GPU quota exhausted causing autoscaler to fail provisioning; provisioner had stuck create ops causing backlog growth and eviction loops. Mitigations applied: route fallback to compact models, reduced token limits for non-enterprise, restarted provisioner controllers, drained noncritical pools, opened quota support. Current status: backlog 2.6k, p95=0.95s, p99=2.8s, no new 5xx from core hosted-api.

jonathan: follow-ups: make autoscaler handle quota-exceeded gracefully (dont spin create ops endlessly), add metric for quota_retries, and add circuit-breaker to provisioner to stop creating new nodes after N consecutive quota errors.

kate: ops task created to revert flag and routing when quota increases or backlog <500 for 30m. ticket: OPS-1229.

maria (oncall): I'll mark this as 'Mitigated' and hand off to infra for next-day postmortem. Oncall will stay for 30m and then hand to infra for deep dive. Thanks all. :white_check_mark:

sre-bot: Incident update: status=mitigated, severity=sev2, owner=maria (oncall), followup=OPS-1229, pm=jonathan.

maria (oncall): filing initial incident note and linking CS communication. We'll capture timeline and action items in postmortem doc.

max: adding note: consider short-term capacity alert that watches cloud quota headroom (threshold 15% remaining) to warn before autoscale fails.

jonathan: agreed. Adding `cloud.quota.gpu_headroom` alert to infra playbook.

customer-success: we sent a brief summary to impacted customers, included expected timeline for SLA credit evaluation.

maria (oncall): handing off to @jonathan and @inge for postmortem next steps. Leaving thread open for any new regressions.

jonathan: taking handoff. tagging infra leads for root cause analysis.

inge: noted. I'll coordinate postmortem and schedule follow-up with CS tomorrow.

ops-bot: Reminder: create postmortem in /incidents/postmortems/OPS-1229 within 24h.

maria (oncall): closing pager for now — will reopen if we see backlog >1k. Good job team. :heart:
__meta_note: This thread is a simulated realistic Slack incident conversation for dataset purposes. It follows agents.md schema: single string messages in chronological order, prefixed by sender name, with metadata fields.
